title: Deep learning on dual-modality ultrasound videos characterizes superficial lymphadenopathy
summary: A multicenter study of 4026 patients with pathologically confirmed lymphadenopathy built DMUVL-DiagNet, which combines B-mode and color Doppler videos with basic clinical information. The abstract reports AUCs of 0.91-0.95 for benign versus malignant and 0.87-0.91 for lymphoma versus metastasis across test sets, including a prospective external video set (n = 454) and an external static image set (n = 1956). Junior radiologist AUCs rose from 0.72 to 0.88 and from 0.58 to 0.77 with model assistance. This is a diagnostic accuracy study, not an outcome study; full text was not reviewed.
ai_technology: DMUVL-DiagNet, a deep learning model that integrates B-mode and color Doppler ultrasound videos with basic clinical information
organization: Lanzhou University Second Hospital; Gansu Province Medical Engineering Research Center for Intelligence Ultrasound

evidence.tested: Trained and internally tested on a retrospective video set (n = 1616); externally tested on a prospective dual-modality video set (n = 454) and a static image set (n = 1956), with a reader study.
evidence.unknown: Whether the model changes clinical decisions or outcomes; performance outside the five participating centers; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Classifies benign versus malignant superficial lymph nodes and lymphoma versus metastasis from ultrasound videos.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
